proposal.title: Between Rooms
proposal.subtitle: The proposal is the first bridge.
proposal.thesis: Let independently governed communities exchange a bounded need, a useful method, a scoped invitation and an inspectable return without surrendering their systems or their authority.

pilot.publicQuestion: How could a locally governed food-access group compare sourcing, a two-hour information table and reusable methods without sharing any resident records?

sequence.name: LISTEN
sequence.meaning: A local steward names the problem. The problem is not invented by a model.

sequence.name: MAP
sequence.meaning: JAR;VIS may research candidates; planZ displays blockers and source lineage.

sequence.name: INVITE
sequence.meaning: A tailored, revocable proposal is offered to one institution. A proposal is not permission.

sequence.name: RECEIVE
sequence.meaning: The receiving institution controls HOLD, REFUSE or review of the specific offer.

sequence.name: ACT
sequence.meaning: Only a separate authorized local decision can permit bounded real work.

sequence.name: REPORT
sequence.meaning: A participant's reported result is testimony, not independent confirmation.

sequence.name: VERIFY
sequence.meaning: An independent, qualified reviewer checks evidence within an agreed scope.

sequence.name: RETURN
sequence.meaning: A public-safe method can be shared only after authorization and review.

safeguards: Each institution and local community retains independent authority.
No institution listed here has joined, endorsed, funded, or even received this proposal by virtue of being listed.
A submitted form, link access, or a simulated acceptance is not verified identity or consent.
Live participants must approve scope, data policy, publication and field actions separately.
No resident records, precise shelter locations, case files, secrets or credentials belong in public bridge packets.
REPORTED != VERIFIED; SIGNED != TRUE; REVIEWED != ADMITTED; PUBLIC != PERMITTED.

doors.name: MIT Solve
doors.alignment: Test whether a working coordination prototype can improve economic resilience and housing support without centralizing local authority.
doors.request: Review a working prototype and connect us to appropriate pilots and technical mentors.
doors.offered: A reproducible synthetic demo, current-source implementation pointers and a testable pilot plan.
doors.gate: Global Challenges require a functioning prototype; an application is not acceptance. The solution must be framed to match housing or economic opportunity, not merely a generic coordination system.
